respuesta.razonamiento: The architecture shows Vizio's data pipeline for ingesting smart TV telemetry, processing it via Kinesis and Firehose into Redshift and S3, and visualizing it with Amazon QuickSight. AWS Aurora is excluded as it was mentioned only as a rejected experiment.
respuesta.nombre: Vizio Smart TV Telemetry Analytics Architecture

nodes.name: Smart TV
nodes.notes: millions of connected devices; sends logs, perf, and user data

nodes.name: Redshift
nodes.notes: data warehouse aggregating billions of events per month

nodes.name: QuickSight
nodes.notes: in-memory SPICE database for custom SQL queries and dashboards

edges.notes: TVs post logs, performance telemetry, and user data directly to Kinesis
edges.respaldo: Drawn arrow from TV icon to Kinesis icon; transcript: 'these TVs are talking directly to Kinesis to ingest or to send their data up to the cloud'.
Drawn arrow from Kinesis to Kinesis Firehose; transcript: 'we will pipe it through Firehose'.
Drawn arrow from Kinesis Firehose to Redshift; transcript: 'Kinesis Firehose takes the data as is and dumps it into Redshift'.

edges.notes: Stores full raw telemetry data into S3 forever
edges.respaldo: Drawn arrow pointing down from Kinesis Firehose to S3; transcript: 'raw data sort of finds its long-term home in S3'.

edges.notes: QuickSight pulls data via custom SQL into SPICE for reports
edges.respaldo: Drawn arrow pointing down from Redshift to QuickSight; transcript: 'download the data from Redshift to the Spice data sets'.
